source.citation: Brudermueller, T. et al. (2025) HEAPO - An Open Dataset for Heat Pump Optimization with Smart Electricity Meter Data and On-Site Inspection Protocols, Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.15056919

split: by home; 20 % dev per (building type x heat-pump type) stratum with >= 3 homes, rest exam; dev only fits the baselines

input.meters: {'elec': hourly kW}: kWh_received_Total summed over the hour (all four quarter-hours present), bad hours (BDG2 electricity flags) NaN; HEAPO has no fuel / district meters
input.T: hourly mean air temperature of the home's HEAPO station (Weather_ID); gaps <= 12 h interpolated, then filled from the nearest value (as realdata.hue_cases)
input.GHI: clear-sky GHI x 0.6 (pvlib, Ineichen, 47.38 N 8.54 E, at the half hour): the stations log sunshine duration, not irradiance
input.window: most complete 365-day window starting on a month boundary (UTC), >= 300 days of good hours
input.flags: BDG2 electricity flags (missing, zero, zero runs >= 24 h, negative, spikes, flatlines >= 24 h, linear-fill runs >= 12 h) make an hour bad; the BDG2 level-shift rule is NOT applied (it flags the heating season of heat-pump homes); its day count is reported per home
input.annual: read_annual({'elec': nanmean(elec_kW) * 8760}, HDD, CDD), HDD/CDD = sum over local days of max(18.33 - Tday, 0) / max(Tday - 18.33, 0) (as realfeats.bdg2)

output_gap: The Detective has no air- vs ground-source output and no emitter output (floor heating / radiators): recorded, not scored. Every home has a heat pump, so the heating class has no negative case.

rows.metric: heated floor area, median abs. % error
single vs multi-family: accuracy of argmax(P(residential_single), P(residential_multi))
rows.unit_set: exam homes with use single or multi
rows.note: info only, no verdict: the exam has 2 multi-family homes (< 10)

rows.metric: share of exam homes with heat_pump as the top heating class; median P(heat_pump)
rows.note: info only (every home has a heat pump)

model_input: released weights/ through Detective.read_hourly(meters, T, GHI, loc, lat), read_monthly_from_hourly and read_annual, from work/exam2/heapo/proc/<home>.parquet; point estimates are the decoded value (floor_area_m2[0], year_built[0]). A round-2 release is scored the same way with its own weights. No refit on these data.

baselines.name: annual elec / dev median kWh per m2 of the TRUE building type
baselines.note: given the true type, which the Detective is not

baselines.name: annual elec / dev median kWh per m2 (all dev homes)
dev-fitted line log10 A = a + b log10 annual kWh (least squares on dev)
dev-fitted line year = a + b log10 annual kWh

baseline_inputs: annual kWh = nanmean(elec_kW) * 8760 over the same window the Detective reads; dev rows with area_row / year_row only

interval.method: 95 % percentile bootstrap over exam homes, paired
interval.statistic: model metric minus the best baseline's metric on the same resample (best = better point value on the full exam row)
interval.verdict: win if entirely on the good side of zero, loss if entirely on the bad side, tie if it spans zero; n homes stated
